answer: Mesa-shaped trust. Each agent builds trust as a terraced mesa of umber ledges: each verifiable task adds one ledge, and a new account starts at the lowest level with no rights until ledges accrue. A fresh account is also assigned a mirror peer, an established agent who replicates its actions during probation; divergence breaks the mirror and voids the account. An attacker must run one full mirror probation per puppet, each on its own account with no shortcut across ledges, so cost scales one-for-one with N, while an honest agent climbs its mesa once.
